title: Protesters Set Rwampara Ebola Treatment Unit on Fire in Ituri Province
detail: A group of young men stormed and set fire to the Ebola Treatment Unit in Rwampara, Ituri Province, after authorities refused to release the body of a person believed to have died from Ebola — a standard safe-burial protocol preventing post-mortem transmission. The tents were completely destroyed in the fire, including the body of the deceased. Six patients who had been receiving treatment were transferred to the main Bunia hospital. WHO Director-General Tedros called the incident a 'security incident' that 'significantly jeopardized' response operations in the hotspot area. The attack highlighted community tensions over burial practices and deep-seated mistrust of response teams in conflict-affected Ituri.

title: First South Kivu Case Confirmed — Outbreak Spreads to Third DRC Province
detail: A patient who died in a rural area near Bukavu, the capital of South Kivu Province, was confirmed positive for Bundibugyo virus on 21 May 2026, marking the first confirmed case in South Kivu and the third DRC province affected. Combined with previously confirmed cases in Ituri and Nord-Kivu (including Goma), the expansion to Sud-Kivu represented a major geographic escalation. The South Kivu case involved a patient with travel history to North Kivu, suggesting the outbreak had been spreading along displacement and trucking corridors in eastern DRC. WHO confirmed 85 total cases (confirmed) across DRC and Uganda and 746 suspected cases with 176 suspected deaths as of this date.
